name: Probing for specific installed apps
plain: Android lets an app declare apps to see; iOS limits canOpenURL to 50 declared schemes.
meaning: Lets an app check for a specific partner app (banking, wallet, rival) without a full list. Both platforms cap the surface.

android.api_surface: PackageManager.getPackageInfo() on declared packages or intents
android.note: Declared in manifest; no hard cap on count but reviewed

ios.revocation: App Review: no probing for fingerprinting
ios.api_surface: Capped at 50 schemes since iOS 9; returns false if scheme is undeclared

limits.headline: Can check if a few named apps are installed, but not list them all
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app starts or when it checks for a partner app
can: Check whether a specific bank, wallet or partner app is on the phone
Open that app if it is there
Guess which apps you use from the short list it chose
cannot: See any app it did not name ahead of time
Check more than 50 app names on iPhone
Hide the check from store review, since the names are listed in the app
limits.differs: Android needs the app names listed in the app before it can check. iPhone allows up to 50 declared link names.

story.what_it_is: An app quietly checks whether a few chosen other apps are on your phone.
story.for_you: You never see this happen. It can make a button say 'Open in Venmo' or hide the Venmo option if you do not have it. It can also be used to guess who you are.
story.for_makers: Apps use it to offer a partner app's checkout or login only when that app exists. Ad tech and fraud systems use it as one more clue about a device, so both platforms limit it.

use_cases.example: A checkout page shows 'Pay with PayPal' only when the PayPal app is installed.
A banking app checks for a known remote access app before it allows a big transfer, as fraud defense.
A sharing menu lists WhatsApp and Messenger only when those apps are present.
A game checks if the publisher's other game is installed and gives a cross promo gift.
A marketing SDK checks for rival apps, such as a competing food delivery app, to tune ads.
Anti cheat tools look for known cheat tools or emulators and block the player from ranked matches.

story.android_note: Android needs the app to list what it wants to see in its own file, and Play reviews that list.
story.ios_note: iOS limits an app to 50 declared schemes and only answers yes or no.
